questions.q: What is the real difference between Fabric Real-Time Intelligence and Databricks Structured Streaming?
options: One of them is simply better than the other in every case
No-code vs. code-first — Fabric's tools are visual and UI-configured, while Databricks Structured Streaming is written as PySpark code
Fabric can't do windowing at all, only Databricks can
Databricks doesn't support watermarks or late data handling
questions.explain: Both solve the identical underlying problem — the difference is how you build it, not what's possible.

questions.q: What is the Databricks Structured Streaming equivalent of Fabric's Window transformation node?
options: Unity Catalog's three-level namespace
The Fabric Monitoring Hub
.groupBy(window(...)) in PySpark
Delta Lake's MERGE INTO command
questions.explain: Both express the same tumbling/hopping/session windowing concepts, just through code instead of a canvas node.

questions.q: Why do Fabric and Databricks end up using almost identical windowing vocabulary despite being built by different teams?
options: Microsoft and Databricks share the same engineering team
Every streaming engine has to solve the exact same set of hard problems, and there are only so many reasonable solutions to each
Fabric copied Databricks's exact source code
It's a pure coincidence with no underlying reason
questions.explain: Learning one gives you almost all of the other, just under a different label.

questions.q: Which Fabric real-time concept has no direct Databricks equivalent, according to this lesson?
options: Watermarks
Activator — Spark alerting instead means writing custom code against a hook like foreachBatch
Eventstream sources
Windowing
questions.explain: Activator's rule-based alerting on objects and properties has no built-in Databricks counterpart.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should a real project actually choose between the two?
options: Based on existing team skills and how much custom code-level control is needed — many real organizations end up using both together
Always choose Databricks, since Fabric can't handle production workloads
Always choose Fabric, since Databricks Structured Streaming is being deprecated
The choice doesn't matter since the two are functionally interchangeable in every respect
questions.explain: A team already comfortable with no-code tools and wanting speed reaches for Fabric; a team needing complex custom logic reaches for Databricks.
